description:
## Goal

Fill in `guides/Getting Started.md` with a narrative walkthrough of the TodoList
example from Track G. The guide is already referenced in `mix.exs` `docs/0`; the
file exists as an empty stub. Do NOT create a new file — fill in the existing one.

The guide teaches: defcomponent, typed props, ~F templates, use_state, event closures
(on_click / on_submit), keyed list rendering, and a rung-2 isolation test. A reader
who finishes this guide can build and test a stateless Filament component from scratch.

## Deviation policy

Any deviation from this spec requires prior approval. Stop work, run
`bw comment <ticket-id> "..."` describing the conflict, reopen the ticket, and await
guidance. Do not improvise.

---

## 0. Prerequisites — read implementations first

Before writing the guide, read:

  - `examples/todo/lib/todo_web/components/todo_item.ex` — real TodoItem component
  - `examples/todo/lib/todo_web/components/todo_list.ex` — real TodoList component
  - `examples/todo/lib/todo/store.ex` — real Todo.Store
  - The actual `defcomponent` macro syntax in `lib/filament/defcomponent.ex`
  - The actual `~F` sigil syntax in `lib/filament/sigil_f.ex`
  - `test/filament/examples/todo_test.exs` (from Track H, flm-yj9.1) — the tests
    that the guide will reference

Quote actual code from these files in the guide. Do NOT invent example code that
differs from what is actually in the examples directory.

---

## 1. File to fill in

FILE: `guides/Getting Started.md`

---

## 2. Guide outline

The guide must contain all of the following sections in order:

### Overview (≤ 150 words)
One paragraph: what Filament is and what this guide covers. State that after reading,
the reader will have a working TodoList component and a passing rung-2 test.

### What you need (≤ 80 words)
Prerequisites: Elixir, Phoenix LiveView, `{:filament, "~> 0.1"}` in deps.
Link to install instructions.

### Defining a component
Introduce `defcomponent` and `prop`. Use the actual `TodoItem` source from
`examples/todo/lib/todo_web/components/todo_item.ex` as the code example.

Explain:
  - `use Filament.Component` (or however the component is defined — read the actual file)
  - `prop :name, :type, opts` (required:, default:)
  - The `~F` sigil for HEEx templates
  - How to reference props with `{@prop_name}` in templates

### Local state with use_state
Introduce `use_state/2`. Use the `TodoList` component's `:filter` and `:new_text`
state declarations as examples. Explain:
  - `{value, setter} = use_state(:key, default)` (or actual return shape — read hooks.ex)
  - Calling `setter.(new_value)` triggers a re-render
  - Rules of hooks (call at top level of render/1 only)

### Event closures
Show the TodoList's on_submit closure for adding items and on_click/on_toggle closures
for toggling items. Explain:
  - How closures are attached in ~F templates (`on_click={fn -> ... end}`)
  - What happens when the user clicks (Filament.LiveView dispatches the closure)
  - The `phx-click="filament:..."` wire format (mention it exists but is internal)

### Composing components and keyed lists
Show the for-comprehension in TodoList that renders `<.TodoItem>` (or `<TodoItem ...>`
— use the actual template syntax from the implementation). Explain:
  - How child components receive props
  - The `:key` attribute on list items and why it matters for reconciliation
  - What happens when a keyed item is removed vs. reordered

### Testing with Filament.Test
Show a rung-2 test from `test/filament/examples/todo_test.exs`. Cover:
  - `Filament.Test.mount/3`
  - `Filament.Test.render_text/1`
  - `Filament.Test.click/2`
  - `Filament.Test.submit/3`
  - Why rung-2 tests need no WebSocket and are fast (`async: true`)

Quote the actual test code from `test/filament/examples/todo_test.exs`. Do not
invent test code — use what H1 actually produced.

### Next steps (≤ 60 words)
Pointers to the Observables guide (I3), the Resource Holds guide (I4), and the API
reference for `Filament.Hooks`.

---

## 3. Style guidelines

- Use present tense, second person ("you").
- Each code block must be fenced with ` ```elixir ` and contain valid Elixir (no
  pseudo-code, no `...` placeholders unless quoting truncated snippets).
- Keep explanations under 200 words per section. This is a how-to, not a reference.
- Target audience: an Elixir/LiveView developer who has not used Filament before.

---

## 4. Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `guides/Getting Started.md` is non-empty (≥ 400 words of prose)
- [ ] All code blocks are valid Elixir (no syntax errors if pasted into iex or a module)
- [ ] All code is quoted from actual example/test implementations, not invented
- [ ] `mix docs` exits 0 and "Getting Started" appears in the generated site
- [ ] The guide mentions defcomponent, prop, use_state, on_click, :key, Filament.Test.mount
- [ ] No broken links or missing module references
